15: # Hausdorff measure and metric (outer) measures
16: 
17: In this file we define the `d`-dimensional Hausdorff measure on an (extended) metric space `X` and
18: the Hausdorff dimension of a set in an (extended) metric space. Let `μ d δ` be the maximal outer
19: measure such that `μ d δ s ≤ (ediam s) ^ d` for every set of diameter less than `δ`. Then
20: the Hausdorff measure `μH[d] s` of `s` is defined as `⨆ δ > 0, μ d δ s`. By Carathéodory's theorem
21: `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric.borel_le_caratheodory`, this is a Borel measure on `X`.
22: 
23: The value of `μH[d]`, `d > 0`, on a set `s` (measurable or not) is given by
24: ```
25: μH[d] s = ⨆ (r : ℝ≥0∞) (hr : 0 < r), ⨅ (t : ℕ → Set X) (hts : s ⊆ ⋃ n, t n)
26:     (ht : ∀ n, ediam (t n) ≤ r), ∑' n, ediam (t n) ^ d
27: ```
28: 
29: For every set `s` and any `d < d'` we have either `μH[d] s = ∞` or `μH[d'] s = 0`, see
30: `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_or_top`. In
31: `Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/HausdorffDimension.lean` we use this fact to define the Hausdorff
32: dimension `dimH` of a set in an (extended) metric space.
33: 
34: We also define two generalizations of the Hausdorff measure. In one generalization (see
35: `MeasureTheory.Measure.mkMetric`) we take any function `m (diam s)` instead of `(diam s) ^ d`. In
36: an even more general definition (see `MeasureTheory.Measure.mkMetric'`) we use any function
37: of `m : Set X → ℝ≥0∞`. Some authors start with a partial function `m` defined only on some sets
38: `s : Set X` (e.g., only on balls or only on measurable sets). This is equivalent to our definition
39: applied to `MeasureTheory.extend m`.
40: 
41: We also define a predicate `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric` which says that an outer measure
42: is additive on metric separated pairs of sets: `μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t` provided that
43: `⨅ (x ∈ s) (y ∈ t), edist x y ≠ 0`. This is the property required for Carathéodory's theorem
44: `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric.borel_le_caratheodory`, so we prove this theorem for any
45: metric outer measure, then prove that outer measures constructed using `mkMetric'` are metric outer
46: measures.
47: 
48: ## Main definitions
49: 
50: * `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric`: an outer measure `μ` is called *metric* if
51:   `μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t` for any two metric separated sets `s` and `t`. A metric outer measure in a
52:   Borel extended metric space is guaranteed to satisfy the Carathéodory condition, see
53:   `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric.borel_le_caratheodory`.
54: * `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.mkMetric'` and its particular case
55:   `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.mkMetric`: a construction of an outer measure that is guaranteed to
56:   be metric. Both constructions are generalizations of the Hausdorff measure. The same measures
57:   interpreted as Borel measures are called `MeasureTheory.Measure.mkMetric'` and
58:   `MeasureTheory.Measure.mkMetric`.
59: * `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure` a.k.a. `μH[d]`: the `d`-dimensional Hausdorff measure.
60:   There are many definitions of the Hausdorff measure that differ from each other by a
61:   multiplicative constant. We put
62:   `μH[d] s = ⨆ r > 0, ⨅ (t : ℕ → Set X) (hts : s ⊆ ⋃ n, t n) (ht : ∀ n, ediam (t n) ≤ r),
63:     ∑' n, ⨆ (ht : ¬Set.Subsingleton (t n)), (ediam (t n)) ^ d`,
64:   see `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply`. In the most interesting case `0 < d` one
65:   can omit the `⨆ (ht : ¬Set.Subsingleton (t n))` part.
66: 
67: ## Main statements
68: 
69: ### Basic properties
70: 
71: * `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric.borel_le_caratheodory`: if `μ` is a metric outer measure
72:   on an extended metric space `X` (that is, it is additive on pairs of metric separated sets), then
73:   every Borel set is Carathéodory measurable (hence, `μ` defines an actual
74:   `MeasureTheory.Measure`). See also `MeasureTheory.Measure.mkMetric`.
75: * `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_mono`: `μH[d] s` is an antitone function
76:   of `d`.
77: * `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_or_top`: if `d₁ < d₂`, then for any `s`, either
78:   `μH[d₂] s = 0` or `μH[d₁] s = ∞`. Together with the previous lemma, this means that `μH[d] s` is
79:   equal to infinity on some ray `(-∞, D)` and is equal to zero on `(D, +∞)`, where `D` is a possibly
80:   infinite number called the *Hausdorff dimension* of `s`; `μH[D] s` can be zero, infinity, or
81:   anything in between.
82: * `MeasureTheory.Measure.nullSingletonClass_hausdorff`: Hausdorff measure has value zero on
83:   singletons.
84: 
85: ### Hausdorff measure in `ℝⁿ`
86: 
87: * `MeasureTheory.hausdorffMeasure_pi_real`: for a nonempty `ι`, `μH[card ι]` on `ι → ℝ` equals
88:   Lebesgue measure.
89: 
90: ## Notation
91: 
92: We use the following notation localized in `MeasureTheory`.
93: 
94: - `μH[d]` : `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure d`
95: 
96: ## Implementation notes
97: 
98: There are a few similar constructions called the `d`-dimensional Hausdorff measure. E.g., some
99: sources only allow coverings by balls and use `r ^ d` instead of `(diam s) ^ d`. While these
100: construction lead to different Hausdorff measures, they lead to the same notion of the Hausdorff
101: dimension.
102: 
103: ## References
104: 
105: * [Herbert Federer, Geometric Measure Theory, Chapter 2.10][Federer1996]
106: 
107: ## Tags
108: 
109: Hausdorff measure, measure, metric measure
110: -/

127: /-!
128: ### Metric outer measures
129: 
130: In this section we define metric outer measures and prove Carathéodory's theorem: a metric outer
131: measure has the Carathéodory property.
132: -/
133: 
134: 
135: /-- We say that an outer measure `μ` in an (e)metric space is *metric* if `μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t`
136: for any two metric separated sets `s`, `t`. -/
137: def IsMetric (μ : OuterMeasure X) : Prop :=
138:   ∀ s t : Set X, Metric.AreSeparated s t → μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t
139: 
140: namespace IsMetric
141: 
142: variable {μ : OuterMeasure X}
143: 
144: /-- A metric outer measure is additive on a finite set of pairwise metric separated sets. -/
145: theorem finset_iUnion_of_pairwise_separated (hm : IsMetric μ) {I : Finset ι} {s : ι → Set X}
146:     (hI : ∀ i ∈ I, ∀ j ∈ I, i ≠ j → Metric.AreSeparated (s i) (s j)) :
147:     μ (⋃ i ∈ I, s i) = ∑ i ∈ I, μ (s i) := by
148:   classical
149:   induction I using Finset.induction_on with
150:   | empty => simp
151:   | insert i I hiI ihI =>
152:     simp only [Finset.mem_insert] at hI
153:     rw [Finset.set_biUnion_insert, hm, ihI, Finset.sum_insert hiI]
154:     exacts [fun i hi j hj hij => hI i (Or.inr hi) j (Or.inr hj) hij,
155:       Metric.AreSeparated.finset_iUnion_right fun j hj =>
156:         hI i (Or.inl rfl) j (Or.inr hj) (ne_of_mem_of_not_mem hj hiI).symm]
157: 
158: /-- **Carathéodory's theorem**. If `m` is a metric outer measure, then every Borel measurable set
159: `t` is Carathéodory measurable: for any (not necessarily measurable) set `s` we have
160: `μ (s ∩ t) + μ (s \ t) = μ s`. -/
161: theorem borel_le_caratheodory (hm : IsMetric μ) : borel X ≤ μ.caratheodory := by
162:   rw [borel_eq_generateFrom_isClosed]
163:   refine MeasurableSpace.generateFrom_le fun t ht => μ.isCaratheodory_iff_le.2 fun s => ?_
164:   set S : ℕ → Set X := fun n => {x ∈ s | (↑n)⁻¹ ≤ infEDist x t}
165:   have Ssep (n) : Metric.AreSeparated (S n) t :=
166:     ⟨n⁻¹, ENNReal.inv_ne_zero.2 (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top _),
167:       fun x hx y hy ↦ hx.2.trans <| infEDist_le_edist_of_mem hy⟩
168:   have Ssep' : ∀ n, Metric.AreSeparated (S n) (s ∩ t) := fun n =>
169:     (Ssep n).mono Subset.rfl inter_subset_right
170:   have S_sub : ∀ n, S n ⊆ s \ t := fun n =>
171:     subset_inter inter_subset_left (Ssep n).subset_compl_right
172:   have hSs : ∀ n, μ (s ∩ t) + μ (S n) ≤ μ s := fun n =>
173:     calc
174:       μ (s ∩ t) + μ (S n) = μ (s ∩ t ∪ S n) := Eq.symm <| hm _ _ <| (Ssep' n).symm
175:       _ ≤ μ (s ∩ t ∪ s \ t) := μ.mono <| union_subset_union_right _ <| S_sub n
176:       _ = μ s := by rw [inter_union_sdiff]
177:   have iUnion_S : ⋃ n, S n = s \ t := by
178:     refine Subset.antisymm (iUnion_subset S_sub) ?_
179:     rintro x ⟨hxs, hxt⟩
180:     rw [mem_iff_infEDist_zero_of_closed ht] at hxt
181:     rcases ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt hxt with ⟨n, hn⟩
182:     exact mem_iUnion.2 ⟨n, hxs, hn.le⟩
183:   /- Now we have `∀ n, μ (s ∩ t) + μ (S n) ≤ μ s` and we need to prove
184:     `μ (s ∩ t) + μ (⋃ n, S n) ≤ μ s`. We can't pass to the limit because
185:     `μ` is only an outer measure. -/
186:   by_cases htop : μ (s \ t) = ∞
187:   · rw [htop, add_top, ← htop]
188:     exact μ.mono sdiff_subset
189:   suffices μ (⋃ n, S n) ≤ ⨆ n, μ (S n) by calc
190:     μ (s ∩ t) + μ (s \ t) = μ (s ∩ t) + μ (⋃ n, S n) := by rw [iUnion_S]
191:     _ ≤ μ (s ∩ t) + ⨆ n, μ (S n) := by gcongr
192:     _ = ⨆ n, μ (s ∩ t) + μ (S n) := ENNReal.add_iSup ..
193:     _ ≤ μ s := iSup_le hSs
194:   /- It suffices to show that `∑' k, μ (S (k + 1) \ S k) ≠ ∞`. Indeed, if we have this,
195:     then for all `N` we have `μ (⋃ n, S n) ≤ μ (S N) + ∑' k, m (S (N + k + 1) \ S (N + k))`
196:     and the second term tends to zero, see `OuterMeasure.iUnion_nat_of_monotone_of_tsum_ne_top`
197:     for details. -/
198:   have : ∀ n, S n ⊆ S (n + 1) := fun n x hx =>
199:     ⟨hx.1, le_trans (ENNReal.inv_le_inv.2 <| Nat.cast_le.2 n.le_succ) hx.2⟩
200:   refine (μ.iUnion_nat_of_monotone_of_tsum_ne_top this ?_).le; clear this

note.fact: For each i in countable K, finitely many intervals indexed by 1≤j≤N_i give a countable family of products. If diam(U_i)=r_i and each interval has length ≤r_i, each product has Euclidean diameter ≤sqrt(2)r_i. For r_i>0 and q>0, N_i≤2/r_i implies N_i(sqrt(2)r_i)^(q+1)≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)r_i^q, also after nonnegative summation.

grounds.reason: K⊆N, the U_i cover E, and 0<r_i≤r≤1 with finite sum of q-costs.
N_i=ceil(1/r_i) is positive and ≤2/r_i; its intervals cover I and have length ≤r_i.
F uses the Euclidean product distance.

note.justification: The pairs (i,j) form a subset of N×N, so are countable. For points in a fixed product both coordinate distances are ≤r_i, and the product distance is therefore ≤sqrt(2)r_i. Monotonicity of positive real powers bounds each cost. The usual real-power laws for positive factors give the displayed termwise identity and inequality; taking suprema of finite subsums yields the series estimate. Product coverage follows by selecting an i covering x and then an interval covering t.

∀ (r : ℝ), 0 < r → r ≤ 1 →
  ∃ (N : ℕ) (J : Fin N → Set ℝ), 0 < N ∧
    (↑N : ℝ) ≤ 2 / r ∧
    GP.unitInterval ⊆ ⋃ j, J j ∧
    (∀ j, Metric.ediam (J j) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal r)
arguments.proof:
intro r hr hr1
let N : ℕ := ⌈1 / r⌉₊
have hN : 0 < N := Nat.ceil_pos.mpr (one_div_pos.mpr hr)
have hNr : 0 < (N : ℝ) := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hN
have hceil : 1 / r ≤ (N : ℝ) := Nat.le_ceil _
have hsize : (N : ℝ) ≤ 2 / r := by
  have h := (Nat.ceil_lt_add_one (le_of_lt (one_div_pos.mpr hr))).le
  have h1 : 1 ≤ 1 / r := (le_div_iff₀ hr).mpr (by simpa using hr1)
  dsimp [N]
  linarith
have hinv : 1 / (N : ℝ) ≤ r := by
  apply (div_le_iff₀ hNr).mpr
  have h := (div_le_iff₀ hr).mp hceil
  nlinarith
let J : Fin N → Set ℝ := fun j => Set.Icc ((j : ℝ) / N) (((j : ℝ) + 1) / N)
refine ⟨N, J, hN, hsize, ?_, ?_⟩
· have cov : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ N → ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ (k : ℝ) / N →
      ∃ j : Fin N, t ∈ J j := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero =>
      intro _ t ht ht'
      have ht0 : t = 0 := by simpa using le_antisymm ht' ht
      subst t
      refine ⟨⟨0, hN⟩, ?_⟩
      simp [J, le_of_lt (one_div_pos.mpr hNr)]
    | succ k ih =>
      intro hk t ht ht'
      by_cases htk : t ≤ (k : ℝ) / N
      · exact ih (by omega) t ht htk
      · refine ⟨⟨k, by omega⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
        · exact (lt_of_not_ge htk).le
        · simpa [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one] using ht'
  intro t ht
  obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := cov N le_rfl t ht.1 (by simpa [ne_of_gt hNr] using ht.2)
  exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨j, hj⟩
· intro j
  rw [J, Real.ediam_Icc]
  apply ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
  calc ((j : ℝ) + 1) / N - (j : ℝ) / N = 1 / N := by ring
       _ ≤ r := hinv

∀ (r : ℝ), 0 < r → r ≤ 1 →
  ∃ (N : ℕ) (J : Fin N → Set ℝ), 0 < N ∧
    (↑N : ℝ) ≤ 2 / r ∧
    GP.unitInterval ⊆ ⋃ j, J j ∧
    (∀ j, Metric.ediam (J j) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal r)
arguments.proof:
intro r hr hr1
let N : ℕ := ⌈1 / r⌉₊
have hN : 0 < N := Nat.ceil_pos.mpr (one_div_pos.mpr hr)
have hNr : 0 < (N : ℝ) := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hN
have hceil : 1 / r ≤ (N : ℝ) := Nat.le_ceil _
have hsize : (N : ℝ) ≤ 2 / r := by
  have h := (Nat.ceil_lt_add_one (le_of_lt (one_div_pos.mpr hr))).le
  have h1 : 1 ≤ 1 / r := (le_div_iff₀ hr).mpr (by simpa using hr1)
  dsimp [N]
  calc _ ≤ 1 / r + 1 := h
       _ ≤ 1 / r + 1 / r := add_le_add_right h1 _
       _ = 2 / r := by ring
have hinv : 1 / (N : ℝ) ≤ r := by
  apply (div_le_iff₀ hNr).mpr
  have h := (div_le_iff₀ hr).mp hceil
  nlinarith
let J : Fin N → Set ℝ := fun j => Set.Icc ((j : ℝ) / N) (((j : ℝ) + 1) / N)
refine ⟨N, J, hN, hsize, ?_, ?_⟩
· have cov : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ N → ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ (k : ℝ) / N →
      ∃ j : Fin N, t ∈ J j := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero =>
      intro _ t ht ht'
      have ht0 : t ≤ 0 := by simpa using ht'
      have ht0 : t = 0 := le_antisymm ht0 ht
      subst t
      refine ⟨⟨0, hN⟩, ?_⟩
      simp [J, le_of_lt (one_div_pos.mpr hNr)]
    | succ k ih =>
      intro hk t ht ht'
      by_cases htk : t ≤ (k : ℝ) / N
      · exact ih (by omega) t ht htk
      · refine ⟨⟨k, by omega⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
        · exact (lt_of_not_ge htk).le
        · simpa [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one] using ht'
  intro t ht
  obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := cov N le_rfl t ht.1 (by simpa [ne_of_gt hNr] using ht.2)
  exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨j, hj⟩
· intro j
  dsimp [J]
  rw [Real.ediam_Icc]
  apply ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
  calc ((j : ℝ) + 1) / N - (j : ℝ) / N = 1 / N := by ring
       _ ≤ r := hinv

  Metric.ediam U ≤ ENNReal.ofReal r → Metric.ediam J ≤ ENNReal.ofReal r →
  Metric.ediam {z : GP.Space (n+1) | GP.horizontal z ∈ U ∧ GP.vertical z ∈ J}
    ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt 2 * r)
arguments.proof:
intro U J r hr hU hJ
apply Metric.ediam_le
intro z hz w hw
rw [edist_dist]
apply ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
have hdU : dist (GP.horizontal z) (GP.horizontal w) ≤ r := by
  have h := Metric.edist_le_of_ediam_le hz.1 hw.1 hU
  rwa [edist_dist, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff hr] at h
have hdJ : dist (GP.vertical z) (GP.vertical w) ≤ r := by
  have h := Metric.edist_le_of_ediam_le hz.2 hw.2 hJ
  rwa [edist_dist, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff hr] at h
have hsq : dist z w ^ 2 =
    dist (GP.horizontal z) (GP.horizontal w) ^ 2 +
      dist (GP.vertical z) (GP.vertical w) ^ 2 := by
  simp only [EuclideanSpace.dist_sq_eq, Fin.sum_univ_castSucc,
    GP.horizontal, GP.vertical, PiLp.toLp_apply]
have hsqrt : Real.sqrt 2 ^ 2 = 2 := Real.sq_sqrt (by norm_num)
have hnon : 0 ≤ Real.sqrt 2 * r := mul_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg _) hr
nlinarith [dist_nonneg (x := z) (y := w),
  dist_nonneg (x := GP.horizontal z) (y := GP.horizontal w),
  dist_nonneg (x := GP.vertical z) (y := GP.vertical w),
  sq_nonneg (r - dist (GP.horizontal z) (GP.horizontal w)),
  sq_nonneg (r - dist (GP.vertical z) (GP.vertical w))]

∀ {X : Type} [MetricSpace X] {ι : Type} [Encodable ι]
    (s δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) (V : ι → Set X),
    A ⊆ ⋃ i, V i → (∀ i, Metric.ediam (V i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ) →
    GP.content s δ A ≤ ∑' i, (Metric.ediam (V i)) ^ s
arguments.proof:
intro X _ ι _ s δ A V hcov hdiam
classical
let U : ℕ → Set X := fun j => ⋃ b ∈ Encodable.decode₂ ι j, V b
have hU : GP.Cover A δ U := by
  constructor
  · simpa only [U, Encodable.iUnion_decode₂] using hcov
  · intro j
    dsimp [U]
    rw [Metric.ediam_iUnion_mem_option]
    exact iSup_le fun b => iSup_le fun _ => hdiam b
calc
  GP.content s δ A ≤ GP.cost s U := iInf_le_of_le U (iInf_le _ hU)
  _ = ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (V i).Nonempty), Metric.ediam (V i) ^ s := by
    exact tsum_iUnion_decode₂ (fun t : Set X => ⨆ (_ : t.Nonempty), Metric.ediam t ^ s)
      (by simp) V
  _ ≤ ∑' i, Metric.ediam (V i) ^ s := ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum (fun i => iSup_le fun _ => le_rfl)

406: /-- The diameter of a set in a metric space. To get controllable behavior even when the diameter
407: should be infinite, we express it in terms of the `ediam` -/
408: noncomputable def diam (s : Set α) : ℝ :=
409:   ENNReal.toReal (ediam s)
410: 
411: /-- The diameter of a set is always nonnegative -/
412: theorem diam_nonneg : 0 ≤ diam s :=
413:   ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
414: 
415: theorem diam_subsingleton (hs : s.Subsingleton) : diam s = 0 := by
416:   simp [diam, ediam_subsingleton hs]
417: 
418: /-- The empty set has zero diameter -/
419: @[simp]
420: theorem diam_empty : diam (∅ : Set α) = 0 :=
421:   diam_subsingleton subsingleton_empty
422: 
423: /-- A singleton has zero diameter -/
424: @[simp]
425: theorem diam_singleton : diam ({x} : Set α) = 0 :=
426:   diam_subsingleton subsingleton_singleton
427: 
428: @[to_additive (attr := simp)]
429: theorem diam_one [One α] : diam (1 : Set α) = 0 :=
430:   diam_singleton
431: 
432: -- Does not work as a simp-lemma, since {x, y} reduces to (insert y {x})
433: theorem diam_pair : diam ({x, y} : Set α) = dist x y := by

435: 
436: -- Does not work as a simp-lemma, since {x, y, z} reduces to (insert z (insert y {x}))
437: theorem diam_triple :

439:   simp only [diam, ediam_triple, dist_edist]

442: /-- If the distance between any two points in a set is bounded by some constant `C`,
443: then `ENNReal.ofReal C` bounds the emetric diameter of this set. -/
444: theorem ediam_le_of_forall_dist_le {C : ℝ} (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, dist x y ≤ C) :
445:     ediam s ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C :=

447: 
448: /-- If the distance between any two points in a set is bounded by some non-negative constant,
449: this constant bounds the diameter. -/
450: theorem diam_le_of_forall_dist_le {C : ℝ} (h₀ : 0 ≤ C) (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, dist x y ≤ C) :
451:     diam s ≤ C :=
452:   ENNReal.toReal_le_of_le_ofReal h₀ (ediam_le_of_forall_dist_le h)
453: 
454: /-- If the distance between any two points in a nonempty set is bounded by some constant,
455: this constant bounds the diameter. -/
456: theorem diam_le_of_forall_dist_le_of_nonempty (hs : s.Nonempty) {C : ℝ}
457:     (h : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, dist x y ≤ C) : diam s ≤ C :=
458:   have h₀ : 0 ≤ C :=
459:     let ⟨x, hx⟩ := hs
460:     le_trans dist_nonneg (h x hx x hx)
461:   diam_le_of_forall_dist_le h₀ h
462: 
463: /-- The distance between two points in a set is controlled by the diameter of the set. -/
464: theorem dist_le_diam_of_mem' (h : ediam s ≠ ⊤) (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) :
465:     dist x y ≤ diam s := by

469: /-- Characterize the boundedness of a set in terms of the finiteness of its emetric.diameter. -/

    (U : ι → Set (GP.Space n)) (d : ι → ℝ),
    0 < q → r ≤ 1 → Real.sqrt 2 * r ≤ δ →
    E ⊆ ⋃ i, U i →
    (∀ i, 0 < d i ∧ d i ≤ r ∧ Metric.ediam (U i) = ENNReal.ofReal (d i)) →
    (∑' i, ENNReal.ofReal ((d i)^q)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ε →
    GP.content (q+1) δ (GP.cylinder E) ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal (2 * (Real.sqrt 2) ^ (q+1) * ε)

classical
have mesh : ∀ (r : ℝ), 0 < r → r ≤ 1 →
  ∃ (N : ℕ) (J : Fin N → Set ℝ), 0 < N ∧
    (↑N : ℝ) ≤ 2 / r ∧
    GP.unitInterval ⊆ ⋃ j, J j ∧
    (∀ j, Metric.ediam (J j) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal r) := by

  let N : ℕ := ⌈1 / r⌉₊
  have hN : 0 < N := Nat.ceil_pos.mpr (one_div_pos.mpr hr)
  have hNr : 0 < (N : ℝ) := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hN
  have hceil : 1 / r ≤ (N : ℝ) := Nat.le_ceil _
  have hsize : (N : ℝ) ≤ 2 / r := by
    have h := (Nat.ceil_lt_add_one (le_of_lt (one_div_pos.mpr hr))).le
    have h1 : 1 ≤ 1 / r := (le_div_iff₀ hr).mpr (by simpa using hr1)
    dsimp [N]
    calc _ ≤ 1 / r + 1 := h
         _ ≤ 1 / r + 1 / r := add_le_add_right h1 _
         _ = 2 / r := by ring
  have hinv : 1 / (N : ℝ) ≤ r := by
    apply (div_le_iff₀ hNr).mpr
    have h := (div_le_iff₀ hr).mp hceil
    nlinarith
  let J : Fin N → Set ℝ := fun j => Set.Icc ((j : ℝ) / N) (((j : ℝ) + 1) / N)
  refine ⟨N, J, hN, hsize, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have cov : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ N → ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ (k : ℝ) / N →
        ∃ j : Fin N, t ∈ J j := by
      intro k
      induction k with
      | zero =>
        intro _ t ht ht'
        have ht0 : t ≤ 0 := by simpa using ht'
        have ht0 : t = 0 := le_antisymm ht0 ht
        subst t
        refine ⟨⟨0, hN⟩, ?_⟩
        simp [J, le_of_lt (one_div_pos.mpr hNr)]
      | succ k ih =>
        intro hk t ht ht'
        by_cases htk : t ≤ (k : ℝ) / N
        · exact ih (by omega) t ht htk
        · refine ⟨⟨k, by omega⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
          · exact (lt_of_not_ge htk).le
          · simpa [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one] using ht'

    obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := cov N le_rfl t ht.1 (by simpa [ne_of_gt hNr] using ht.2)
    exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨j, hj⟩

    dsimp [J]
    rw [Real.ediam_Icc]
    apply ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
    calc ((j : ℝ) + 1) / N - (j : ℝ) / N = 1 / N := by ring
         _ ≤ r := hinv

  Metric.ediam U ≤ ENNReal.ofReal r → Metric.ediam J ≤ ENNReal.ofReal r →
  Metric.ediam {z : GP.Space (n+1) | GP.horizontal z ∈ U ∧ GP.vertical z ∈ J}

  intro z hz w hw
  rw [edist_dist]

  have hdU : dist (GP.horizontal z) (GP.horizontal w) ≤ r := by

    rwa [edist_dist, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff hr] at h

    have h := Metric.edist_le_of_ediam_le hz.2 hw.2 hJ
    rwa [edist_dist, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff hr] at h

    simp only [EuclideanSpace.dist_sq_eq, Fin.sum_univ_castSucc,
      GP.horizontal, GP.vertical, PiLp.toLp_apply]
  have hsqrt : Real.sqrt 2 ^ 2 = 2 := Real.sq_sqrt (by norm_num)
  have hnon : 0 ≤ Real.sqrt 2 * r := mul_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg _) hr
  have hU2 : dist (GP.horizontal z) (GP.horizontal w) ^ 2 ≤ r ^ 2 := by
    nlinarith [dist_nonneg (x := GP.horizontal z) (y := GP.horizontal w)]
  have hJ2 : dist (GP.vertical z) (GP.vertical w) ^ 2 ≤ r ^ 2 := by
    nlinarith [dist_nonneg (x := GP.vertical z) (y := GP.vertical w)]
  have h2 : dist z w ^ 2 ≤ (Real.sqrt 2 * r) ^ 2 := by
    rw [mul_pow, hsqrt]
    linarith

    A ⊆ ⋃ i, V i → (∀ i, Metric.ediam (V i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ) →

      exact tsum_iUnion_decode₂ (fun t : Set X => ⨆ (_ : t.Nonempty), Metric.ediam t ^ s)

  intro q r N hr hN

  have hNr : (N : ℝ) * r ≤ 2 := (le_div_iff₀ hr).mp hN

    rw [Real.mul_rpow hs.le hr.le, Real.rpow_add hr, Real.rpow_one]
    ring
  have hreal : (N : ℝ) * (Real.sqrt 2 * r) ^ (q+1) ≤
      (2 * (Real.sqrt 2) ^ (q+1)) * r^q := by
    rw [heq]
    calc (N : ℝ) * ((Real.sqrt 2)^(q+1) * r^q * r) =
        ((N : ℝ)*r) * ((Real.sqrt 2)^(q+1) * r^q) := by ring
         _ ≤ 2 * ((Real.sqrt 2)^(q+1) * r^q) :=
           mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hNr (by positivity)
         _ = _ := by ring
  have hcast : (N : ℝ≥0∞) = ENNReal.ofReal (N : ℝ) := by simp
  rw [hcast, ENNReal.ofReal_rpow_of_pos (mul_pos hs hr),
    ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (Nat.cast_nonneg N),
    ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by positivity)]
  exact ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal hreal

  fun i => mesh (d i) (hd i).1 ((hd i).2.1.trans hr1)

  intro p

    (hd p.1).2.2.le (hJdiam p.1 p.2)
have hVcov : GP.cylinder E ⊆ ⋃ p, V p := by
  intro z hz
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion.mp (hcov hz.1)
  obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion.mp (hJcov i hz.2)
  exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨⟨i,j⟩, hi, hj⟩

  GP.content (q+1) δ (GP.cylinder E) ≤
      ∑' p, Metric.ediam (V p) ^ (q+1) :=
    compress (q+1) δ (GP.cylinder E) V hVcov (fun p =>
      (hVdiam p).trans (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
        ((mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hd p.1).2.1 (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)).trans hrδ)))
  _ ≤ ∑' p : Σ i, Fin (N i), ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt 2 * d p.1) ^ (q+1) :=
    ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum (fun p => ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow (hVdiam p) (by linarith))
  _ = ∑' i, (N i : ℝ≥0∞) * ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt 2 * d i) ^ (q+1) := by
    rw [ENNReal.tsum_sigma]
    simp only [tsum_fintype, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]
  _ ≤ ∑' i, ENNReal.ofReal (2 * (Real.sqrt 2)^(q+1)) * ENNReal.ofReal ((d i)^q) :=
    ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum (fun i => numerical q (d i) (N i) (hd i).1 (hsize i))
  _ = ENNReal.ofReal (2 * (Real.sqrt 2)^(q+1)) * ∑' i, ENNReal.ofReal ((d i)^q) :=
    ENNReal.tsum_mul_left
  _ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 * (Real.sqrt 2)^(q+1)) * ENNReal.ofReal ε :=
    mul_le_mul_left' hsum _

    (ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by positivity)).symm

have mesh : ∀ (r : ℝ), 0 < r → r ≤ 1 →
  ∃ (N : ℕ) (J : Fin N → Set ℝ), 0 < N ∧

    GP.unitInterval ⊆ ⋃ j, J j ∧
    (∀ j, Metric.ediam (J j) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal r) := by

  let N : ℕ := ⌈1 / r⌉₊

  · have cov : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ N → ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ (k : ℝ) / N →

          · simpa [Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one] using ht'

    rw [Real.ediam_Icc]
    apply ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
    calc ((j : ℝ) + 1) / N - (j : ℝ) / N = 1 / N := by ring

  fun i => mesh (d i) (hd i).1 ((hd i).2.1.trans hr1)

    (hd p.1).2.2.le (hJdiam p.1 p.2)
have hVcov : GP.cylinder E ⊆ ⋃ p, V p := by
  intro z hz
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion.mp (hcov hz.1)
  obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion.mp (hJcov i hz.2)
  exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨⟨i,j⟩, hi, hj⟩
calc
  GP.content (q+1) δ (GP.cylinder E) ≤
      ∑' p, Metric.ediam (V p) ^ (q+1) :=
    compress (q+1) δ (GP.cylinder E) V hVcov (fun p =>
      (hVdiam p).trans (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
        ((mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hd p.1).2.1 (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)).trans hrδ)))
  _ ≤ ∑' p : Σ i, Fin (N i), ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt 2 * d p.1) ^ (q+1) :=
    ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum (fun p => ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow (hVdiam p) (by linarith))
  _ = ∑' i, (N i : ℝ≥0∞) * ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt 2 * d i) ^ (q+1) := by
    rw [ENNReal.tsum_sigma' (fun p : Σ i, Fin (N i) =>
      ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt 2 * d p.1) ^ (q+1))]
    simp only [tsum_fintype, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]
  _ ≤ ∑' i, ENNReal.ofReal (2 * (Real.sqrt 2)^(q+1)) * ENNReal.ofReal ((d i)^q) :=
    ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum (fun i => numerical q (d i) (N i) (hd i).1 (hsize i))

    ENNReal.tsum_mul_left

    mul_le_mul_left' hsum _
